name: P1 · General English
description: 3 of 13 topics so far (6 sets × 20 questions): Parts of Speech; Verbs – Tense, Time and Aspect; Auxiliaries and Modals. More topics are added to this pack as the plan goes on; re-importing only adds the new sets.

questions.question: In the sentence 'A flock of sheep was grazing on the hill', the word 'flock' is a:
questions.subject: Nouns, Pronouns and Adjectives
questions.explanation: A collective noun names a group taken as one whole.

questions.question: Which of the following is an abstract noun?
questions.subject: Nouns, Pronouns and Adjectives
questions.explanation: Abstract nouns name qualities, states or actions that cannot be touched.

questions.question: The plural of 'passer-by' is:
questions.subject: Nouns, Pronouns and Adjectives
questions.explanation: In compound nouns the main word takes the plural: mothers-in-law, commanders-in-chief.

questions.question: The plural of 'criterion' is:
questions.subject: Nouns, Pronouns and Adjectives
questions.explanation: Similarly phenomenon → phenomena.

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.

options.C: He gave me a piece of advice.

questions.subject: Nouns, Pronouns and Adjectives
questions.explanation: 'Advice' is uncountable; so are furniture, information and luggage.

questions.question: In 'The boy who won the prize is my cousin', the word 'who' is a:
questions.subject: Nouns, Pronouns and Adjectives
questions.explanation: It joins the clause to the noun 'boy'; in 'Who is there?' it would be interrogative.

questions.question: In 'I myself saw the accident', the word 'myself' is used as a/an:
questions.subject: Nouns, Pronouns and Adjectives
questions.explanation: It emphasises 'I'. In 'I hurt myself' it is reflexive (object of the verb).

questions.question: Choose the correct option: 'This is a secret between you and ___.'
questions.subject: Nouns, Pronouns and Adjectives
questions.explanation: After a preposition the object form is needed.

questions.question: Choose the correct option: 'Each of the students must bring ___ own book.'
questions.subject: Nouns, Pronouns and Adjectives
questions.explanation: 'Each' is singular, so a singular possessive is traditional (Wren & Martin).

questions.question: In 'This book is mine' and 'This is my book', the word 'this' is respectively a:
questions.subject: Nouns, Pronouns and Adjectives
questions.explanation: Before a noun it qualifies the noun; standing alone it replaces the noun.

questions.question: Choose the correct order of adjectives:

options.A: a red old beautiful Italian car
options.B: a beautiful old red Italian car
options.C: an old beautiful Italian red car
options.D: an Italian red old beautiful car

questions.subject: Nouns, Pronouns and Adjectives
questions.explanation: Usual order: opinion – size – age – shape – colour – origin – material – purpose.

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence comparing two persons.

options.A: She is more intelligenter of the two sisters.
options.B: She is the intelligentest of the two sisters.
options.C: She is the most intelligent of the two sisters.
options.D: She is the more intelligent of the two sisters.

questions.subject: Nouns, Pronouns and Adjectives
questions.explanation: With two persons the comparative degree is used.

questions.question: 'He has ___ friends, so he never feels lonely.' Choose the right word.
questions.subject: Nouns, Pronouns and Adjectives
questions.explanation: 'A few' (some) is positive; 'few' means hardly any; 'little' is used with uncountable nouns.

questions.question: Choose the correct form: 'The ___ toys were scattered on the floor.'
questions.subject: Nouns, Pronouns and Adjectives
questions.explanation: 'Children' is a plural not ending in s, so it takes 's.

questions.question: Identify the adjective in: 'The tall boy runs very fast.'
questions.subject: Nouns, Pronouns and Adjectives
questions.explanation: 'Tall' describes the noun boy; 'fast' here tells how he runs (adverb).

questions.question:
Match the noun with its kind:
a. Delhi
b. Iron
c. Army
d. Kindness

1. Abstract
2. Material
3. Collective
4. Proper
questions.subject: Nouns, Pronouns and Adjectives
questions.explanation: Proper nouns name particular persons or places; material nouns name substances.

questions.question:
Consider the statements:
I. In 'She is taller than I (am)', the pronoun 'I' is correct.
II. 'Everyone have finished their work' is grammatically correct.
Which is/are correct?
questions.subject: Nouns, Pronouns and Adjectives
questions.explanation: 'Everyone' takes a singular verb: 'Everyone has finished …'.

questions.question:
Assertion (A): 'Furniture' has no plural form 'furnitures'.
Reason (R): 'Furniture' is an uncountable noun.

options.A: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
options.B: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
options.C: A is true, but R is false
options.D: A is false, but R is true

questions.subject: Nouns, Pronouns and Adjectives
questions.explanation: Uncountable nouns are not normally used in the plural; we say 'pieces of furniture'.

questions.question:
Assertion (A): 'Mathematics' is followed by a plural verb, as in 'Mathematics are difficult'.
Reason (R): 'Mathematics' ends in -s.

options.A: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
options.B: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
options.C: A is true, but R is false
options.D: A is false, but R is true

questions.subject: Nouns, Pronouns and Adjectives
questions.explanation: Though it ends in -s, it is a singular subject name: 'Mathematics is difficult'. R is true, A is false.

questions.question:
Assertion (A): In 'The rich are not always happy', 'rich' is used as a noun.
Reason (R): An adjective preceded by 'the' can stand for a whole class of people.

options.A: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
options.B: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
options.C: A is true, but R is false
options.D: A is false, but R is true

questions.subject: Nouns, Pronouns and Adjectives
questions.explanation: 'The rich' means rich people; similarly 'the poor', 'the blind'.

sets.name: 2 · Verbs, Adverbs, Prepositions, Conjunctions and Interjections

questions.question: In 'The baby slept peacefully', the verb 'slept' is:
questions.subject: Verbs, Adverbs, Prepositions, Conjunctions and Interjections
questions.explanation: It has no object; 'peacefully' is an adverb of manner.

questions.question: In 'She has finished her work', the word 'has' is a/an:
questions.subject: Verbs, Adverbs, Prepositions, Conjunctions and Interjections
questions.explanation: 'Finished' is the main verb; 'has' helps to form the present perfect.

questions.question: In 'He seems tired', the verb 'seems' is a:
questions.subject: Verbs, Adverbs, Prepositions, Conjunctions and Interjections
questions.explanation: It links the subject to a word describing it.

questions.question: In 'Swimming is a good exercise', the word 'swimming' is a:

options.A: Present participle used as an adjective

questions.subject: Verbs, Adverbs, Prepositions, Conjunctions and Interjections
questions.explanation: It is the subject of the sentence, so it works as a noun.

questions.question: Identify the kind of adverb in 'He will come tomorrow.'
questions.subject: Verbs, Adverbs, Prepositions, Conjunctions and Interjections
questions.explanation: 'Tomorrow' tells when.

questions.question: In which sentence is 'fast' used as a verb?

options.D: The colours are fast and will not fade.

questions.subject: Verbs, Adverbs, Prepositions, Conjunctions and Interjections
questions.explanation: The same word can be different parts of speech depending on its use.

questions.question: 'He works hard' and 'He hardly works' mean:

options.A: He works with effort; he does almost no work
options.C: He works a lot; he works a lot slowly
options.D: Both mean he does not work

questions.subject: Verbs, Adverbs, Prepositions, Conjunctions and Interjections
questions.explanation: 'Hardly' means scarcely; it is not the adverb form of 'hard'.

questions.question: Choose the correct preposition: 'She is good ___ mathematics.'
questions.subject: Verbs, Adverbs, Prepositions, Conjunctions and Interjections
questions.explanation: The fixed expression is 'good at'.

questions.question: Choose the correct preposition: 'Divide the sweets ___ the four children.'
questions.subject: Verbs, Adverbs, Prepositions, Conjunctions and Interjections
questions.explanation: 'Between' is used for two; 'among' for more than two.

questions.question: Choose the correct option: 'He has been living here ___ 2015.'
questions.subject: Verbs, Adverbs, Prepositions, Conjunctions and Interjections
questions.explanation: 'Since' marks a point of time; 'for' marks a period (for ten years).

questions.question: Choose the correct option: 'I prefer tea ___ coffee.'
questions.subject: Verbs, Adverbs, Prepositions, Conjunctions and Interjections
questions.explanation: 'Prefer' takes 'to', not 'than'.

questions.question: Which of the following is a pair of correlative conjunctions?
questions.subject: Verbs, Adverbs, Prepositions, Conjunctions and Interjections
questions.explanation: Correlatives work in pairs: either … or, not only … but also, both … and.

questions.question: Choose the correct verb: 'Neither Ravi nor his friends ___ come yet.'
questions.subject: Verbs, Adverbs, Prepositions, Conjunctions and Interjections
questions.explanation: With neither … nor, the verb agrees with the nearer subject ('friends').

questions.question: In 'I stayed at home because it was raining', the word 'because' is a:
questions.subject: Verbs, Adverbs, Prepositions, Conjunctions and Interjections
questions.explanation: It introduces a dependent (adverb) clause of reason.

questions.question: 'Alas! He is no more.' The word 'Alas' is an interjection expressing:
questions.subject: Verbs, Adverbs, Prepositions, Conjunctions and Interjections
questions.explanation: 'Hurrah!' expresses joy; 'Bravo!' approval.

questions.question:
Match the word in the sentence with its part of speech:
a. 'He walked AFTER me.'
b. 'He came AFTER I had left.'
c. 'He came soon AFTER.'
d. 'In AFTER years he became rich.'

1. Preposition
2. Adverb
3. Conjunction
4. Adjective
questions.subject: Verbs, Adverbs, Prepositions, Conjunctions and Interjections
questions.explanation: A word's part of speech depends on its function in the sentence (Wren & Martin).

questions.question:
Consider the statements:
I. 'And', 'but', 'or' and 'so' are coordinating conjunctions.
II. 'Although' is a coordinating conjunction.
Which is/are correct?
questions.subject: Verbs, Adverbs, Prepositions, Conjunctions and Interjections
questions.explanation: 'Although' introduces a subordinate clause.

questions.question:
Assertion (A): In 'She sings beautifully', 'beautifully' is an adverb.
Reason (R): It modifies the verb 'sings', telling how she sings.

options.A: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
options.B: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
options.C: A is true, but R is false
options.D: A is false, but R is true

questions.subject: Verbs, Adverbs, Prepositions, Conjunctions and Interjections
questions.explanation: Adverbs of manner answer the question 'how?'.

questions.question:
Assertion (A): 'The book is on the table' contains a preposition.
Reason (R): A preposition always comes at the end of a sentence.

options.A: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
options.B: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
options.C: A is true, but R is false
options.D: A is false, but R is true

questions.subject: Verbs, Adverbs, Prepositions, Conjunctions and Interjections
questions.explanation: A is true ('on'). R is false: prepositions usually come before a noun or pronoun.

questions.question:
Assertion (A): In 'Birds fly', the verb 'fly' is intransitive.
Reason (R): Some verbs can be used both transitively and intransitively.

options.A: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
options.B: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
options.C: A is true, but R is false
options.D: A is false, but R is true

questions.subject: Verbs, Adverbs, Prepositions, Conjunctions and Interjections
questions.explanation: Both true; 'fly' is intransitive here because it has no object, not because some verbs can be used both ways.

questions.question: Choose the correct form: 'She ___ to school by bus every day.'
questions.subject: Present and Past Tenses
questions.explanation: The simple present is used for habits and routines.

questions.question: Choose the correct form: 'Look! The children ___ in the rain.'
questions.subject: Present and Past Tenses
questions.explanation: The present continuous is used for an action happening now.

questions.question: Choose the correct form: 'I ___ the answer to this question now.'
questions.subject: Present and Past Tenses
questions.explanation: Stative verbs such as know, like and believe are not normally used in continuous forms.

questions.question: Choose the correct form: 'The sun ___ in the east.'
questions.subject: Present and Past Tenses
questions.explanation: Universal truths take the simple present.

questions.question: Choose the correct form: 'I ___ my homework already, so I can play now.'
questions.subject: Present and Past Tenses
questions.explanation: The present perfect links a past action with the present.

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence about a finished past event.
questions.subject: Present and Past Tenses
questions.explanation: The present perfect is not used with a definite past time such as yesterday.

questions.question: Choose the correct form: 'She ___ for two hours and is still at her desk.'
questions.subject: Present and Past Tenses
questions.explanation: The present perfect continuous shows an action continuing up to now.

questions.question: Choose the correct word: 'They have lived in Mysuru ___ 2010.'
questions.subject: Present and Past Tenses
questions.explanation: 'Since' + a point in time; 'for' + a period.

questions.question: Choose the correct form: 'I ___ dinner when the phone rang.'
questions.subject: Present and Past Tenses
questions.explanation: The past continuous shows an action in progress, interrupted by a short past action.

questions.question: Choose the correct form: 'When we reached the station, the train ___.'
questions.subject: Present and Past Tenses
questions.explanation: The past perfect shows the earlier of two past actions.

questions.question: Choose the correct negative: 'He ___ yet.'
questions.subject: Present and Past Tenses
questions.explanation: 'Yet' is typical with the present perfect in negatives and questions.

questions.question: Choose the correct question.

options.A: Did she went to the market?
options.B: Does she went to the market?
options.C: Did she go to the market?
options.D: Did she gone to the market?

questions.subject: Present and Past Tenses
questions.explanation: After did, the base form of the verb is used.

questions.question: Name the tense of: 'They had been waiting for an hour when the bus came.'
questions.subject: Present and Past Tenses
questions.explanation: had been + -ing.

questions.question:
Match the sentence with its tense:
a. I write.
b. I am writing.
c. I have written.
d. I wrote.

1. Simple past
2. Present continuous
3. Present perfect
4. Simple present
questions.subject: Present and Past Tenses
questions.explanation: Each combines a tense (present/past) with an aspect.

questions.question: Choose the correct form: 'Water ___ at 100 °C at sea level.'
questions.subject: Present and Past Tenses
questions.explanation: Scientific facts take the simple present.

questions.question:
Consider the statements:
I. 'She has been living here since 2015' shows an action continuing up to now.
II. 'She lived here since 2015' is correct standard English.
Which is/are correct?
questions.subject: Present and Past Tenses
questions.explanation: 'Since' with a situation continuing to now needs a perfect form.

questions.question:
Consider the statements:
I. The past continuous describes an action in progress at a moment in the past.
II. The past perfect shows the earlier of two past actions.
Which is/are correct?
questions.subject: Present and Past Tenses
questions.explanation: Both are standard uses.

questions.question:
Assertion (A): 'I am knowing him for many years' is incorrect.
Reason (R): 'Know' is a stative verb, not normally used in continuous forms.

options.A: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
options.B: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
options.C: A is true, but R is false
options.D: A is false, but R is true

questions.subject: Present and Past Tenses
questions.explanation: The correct form is 'I have known him for many years'.

questions.question:
Assertion (A): 'I have seen him yesterday' is correct.
Reason (R): The present perfect is not used with a definite past time expression such as 'yesterday'.

options.A: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
options.B: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
options.C: A is true, but R is false
options.D: A is false, but R is true

questions.subject: Present and Past Tenses
questions.explanation: R is the rule, which shows A is incorrect.

questions.question:
Assertion (A): The simple present is used for universal truths.
Reason (R): The simple present always refers to actions happening at the moment of speaking.

options.A: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
options.B: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
options.C: A is true, but R is false
options.D: A is false, but R is true

questions.subject: Present and Past Tenses
questions.explanation: A is true; R is false – actions happening now take the present continuous.

sets.name: 2 · Future Time, Aspect and Sequence of Tenses

questions.question: Strictly by the form of the verb, English has how many tenses?

options.B: Two – present and past; future time is shown with helpers such as will

questions.subject: Future Time, Aspect and Sequence of Tenses
questions.explanation: Many grammarians (e.g. Quirk, Swan) distinguish tense (present/past) from aspect (progressive/perfect).

questions.question: In grammar, 'aspect' shows:

options.A: Whether the subject is singular or plural
options.C: How an action is viewed in time – for example as ongoing (progressive) or completed (perfect)
options.D: The mood of the speaker only

questions.subject: Future Time, Aspect and Sequence of Tenses
questions.explanation: Tense locates an action in time; aspect describes its progress or completion.

questions.question: The sentence 'She has been writing' combines:

options.A: The perfect and progressive aspects in the present tense
options.B: The simple aspect in the past tense

questions.subject: Future Time, Aspect and Sequence of Tenses
questions.explanation: have been + -ing = present perfect progressive.

questions.question: Choose the correct form: 'Look at those dark clouds! It ___ rain.'
questions.subject: Future Time, Aspect and Sequence of Tenses
questions.explanation: 'Be going to' predicts from present evidence.

questions.question: Choose the correct form: 'I ___ my uncle in Hubballi tomorrow; I have already bought the ticket.'
questions.subject: Future Time, Aspect and Sequence of Tenses
questions.explanation: The present continuous is used for fixed personal arrangements.

questions.question: Choose the correct form: 'The train ___ at 6.30 tomorrow morning.'
questions.subject: Future Time, Aspect and Sequence of Tenses
questions.explanation: The simple present is used for timetables and schedules.

questions.question: Choose the correct form: 'By next March, I ___ my degree.'
questions.subject: Future Time, Aspect and Sequence of Tenses
questions.explanation: The future perfect shows completion before a future time.

questions.question: Choose the correct form: 'This time tomorrow, we ___ to Mysuru.'
questions.subject: Future Time, Aspect and Sequence of Tenses
questions.explanation: The future continuous shows an action in progress at a future moment.

questions.question: Choose the correct form: 'I will call you when I ___ home.'
questions.subject: Future Time, Aspect and Sequence of Tenses
questions.explanation: In time clauses about the future, the simple present is used.

questions.question: Choose the correct form: 'If it ___ tomorrow, the match will be cancelled.'
questions.subject: Future Time, Aspect and Sequence of Tenses
questions.explanation: First conditional: if + simple present, will + base verb.

questions.question: Choose the correct reported form: He said, 'I am tired.' → He said that he ___ tired.
questions.subject: Future Time, Aspect and Sequence of Tenses
questions.explanation: After a past reporting verb, the present usually shifts to the past (sequence of tenses).

questions.question: Choose the correct reported form: The teacher said, 'The earth revolves round the sun.' → The teacher said that the earth ___ round the sun.
questions.subject: Future Time, Aspect and Sequence of Tenses
questions.explanation: Universal truths keep the present tense in reported speech.

questions.question: Choose the correct reported form: She said, 'I saw the film yesterday.' → She said that she ___ the film the day before.
questions.subject: Future Time, Aspect and Sequence of Tenses
questions.explanation: The simple past shifts to the past perfect.

questions.question: Choose the correct form: 'By June, she ___ at this school for ten years.'
questions.subject: Future Time, Aspect and Sequence of Tenses
questions.explanation: The future perfect continuous stresses duration up to a future point.

questions.question: 'Shall I open the window?' is used mainly to:

options.D: Make an offer or ask for a suggestion

questions.subject: Future Time, Aspect and Sequence of Tenses
questions.explanation: 'Shall' with I/we in questions offers help or asks for advice.

questions.question:
Match the future form with its typical use:
a. will
b. be going to
c. present continuous
d. simple present

1. Instant decisions, promises and predictions
2. Fixed personal arrangements
3. Timetables and schedules
4. Predictions from present evidence and intentions
questions.subject: Future Time, Aspect and Sequence of Tenses
questions.explanation: English uses several forms to talk about the future.

questions.question:
Consider the statements:
I. English refers to future time with will, be going to and the present continuous, among other forms.
II. The future perfect describes an action that will be completed before a point in the future.
Which is/are correct?
questions.subject: Future Time, Aspect and Sequence of Tenses
questions.explanation: Both statements are correct.

questions.question:
Assertion (A): 'I will call you when I will reach home' is incorrect.
Reason (R): In time clauses referring to the future, the simple present is used instead of will.

options.A: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
options.B: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
options.C: A is true, but R is false
options.D: A is false, but R is true

questions.subject: Future Time, Aspect and Sequence of Tenses
questions.explanation: Correct: 'I will call you when I reach home'.

questions.question:
Assertion (A): 'The train leaves at six tomorrow' is correct English.
Reason (R): 'Will' can be contracted to 'll.

options.A: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
options.B: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
options.C: A is true, but R is false
options.D: A is false, but R is true

questions.subject: Future Time, Aspect and Sequence of Tenses
questions.explanation: Both true, but the sentence is correct because timetables take the simple present.

questions.question:
Assertion (A): In formal reported speech, 'He said that he is ill' follows the usual sequence of tenses.
Reason (R): A past reporting verb is normally followed by a past tense in the reported clause.

options.A: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
options.B: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
options.C: A is true, but R is false
options.D: A is false, but R is true

questions.subject: Future Time, Aspect and Sequence of Tenses
questions.explanation: By the rule in R, the usual form is 'He said that he was ill', so A is false.

sets.name: 1 · Primary Auxiliaries: Be, Have and Do

questions.question: The three primary auxiliary verbs in English are:
questions.subject: Primary Auxiliaries: Be, Have and Do
questions.explanation: They can also be used as main verbs.

questions.question: In 'She is writing a letter', the word 'is' is:

options.C: A primary auxiliary forming the progressive

questions.subject: Primary Auxiliaries: Be, Have and Do
questions.explanation: Be + -ing forms the continuous (progressive) aspect.

questions.question: In 'They have finished their work', 'have' is used to form the:
questions.subject: Primary Auxiliaries: Be, Have and Do
questions.explanation: Have + past participle forms the perfect aspect.

questions.question: In 'He has a new bicycle', 'has' is used as a:
questions.subject: Primary Auxiliaries: Be, Have and Do
questions.explanation: There is no other verb in the sentence.

questions.question: In 'The letter was posted yesterday', 'was' helps to form the:
questions.subject: Primary Auxiliaries: Be, Have and Do
questions.explanation: Be + past participle forms the passive.

questions.question: Choose the correct negative form of 'She likes coffee':
questions.subject: Primary Auxiliaries: Be, Have and Do
questions.explanation: Do-support: does + not + base form.

questions.question: Choose the correct question form of 'They went to Mysuru':
questions.subject: Primary Auxiliaries: Be, Have and Do
questions.explanation: After 'did', the main verb is in its base form.

questions.question: In 'I DO want to help you', the auxiliary 'do' is used for:
questions.subject: Primary Auxiliaries: Be, Have and Do
questions.explanation: Emphatic 'do' is stressed in speech.

questions.question: Fill in the blank: 'Neither of the boys ___ present yesterday.'
questions.subject: Primary Auxiliaries: Be, Have and Do
questions.explanation: 'Neither' takes a singular verb in formal English.

questions.question: Fill in the blank: 'The children ___ been playing since morning.'
questions.subject: Primary Auxiliaries: Be, Have and Do
questions.explanation: Plural subject + have been + -ing (present perfect continuous).

questions.question: Choose the correct question tag: 'She is a teacher, ___?'
questions.subject: Primary Auxiliaries: Be, Have and Do
questions.explanation: Positive statement → negative tag with the same auxiliary.

questions.question: Choose the correct question tag: 'You didn't call me, ___?'
questions.subject: Primary Auxiliaries: Be, Have and Do
questions.explanation: Negative statement → positive tag.

questions.question: Choose the correct question tag: 'I am late, ___?'
questions.subject: Primary Auxiliaries: Be, Have and Do
questions.explanation: 'Aren't I' is the standard tag for 'I am'.

questions.question: Choose the correct question tag: 'Let's go for a walk, ___?'
questions.subject: Primary Auxiliaries: Be, Have and Do
questions.explanation: Suggestions with 'Let's' take 'shall we'.

questions.question: Choose the correct question tag: 'Everyone has arrived, ___?'
questions.subject: Primary Auxiliaries: Be, Have and Do
questions.explanation: Indefinite pronouns like 'everyone' take 'they' in tags.

questions.question: Identify the sentence in which 'do' is a MAIN verb:

options.C: He does his homework every evening.

questions.subject: Primary Auxiliaries: Be, Have and Do
questions.explanation: Here 'does' means 'performs'; in the others it is an auxiliary.

questions.question:
Match the use of the auxiliary with the example:
a. Progressive
b. Perfect
c. Passive
d. Emphasis

1. She has left.
2. The bridge was built in 2010.
3. They are singing.
4. I did lock the door.
questions.subject: Primary Auxiliaries: Be, Have and Do
questions.explanation: Be, have and do each have typical uses.

questions.question:
Consider the statements:
I. 'Have' can be used both as an auxiliary and as a main verb.
II. After the auxiliary 'did', the main verb takes its past form.
Which is/are correct?
questions.subject: Primary Auxiliaries: Be, Have and Do
questions.explanation: After 'did' the main verb is in its base form: 'Did he go?'

questions.question:
Assertion (A): 'He doesn't knows the answer' is incorrect.
Reason (R): After 'does', the main verb is used in its base form.

options.A: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
options.B: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
options.C: A is true, but R is false
options.D: A is false, but R is true

questions.subject: Primary Auxiliaries: Be, Have and Do
questions.explanation: Correct: 'He doesn't know the answer.'

questions.question:
Assertion (A): 'Be' is used to form the perfect tenses.
Reason (R): 'Be' is used to form the passive voice.

options.A: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
options.B: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
options.C: A is true, but R is false
options.D: A is false, but R is true

questions.subject: Primary Auxiliaries: Be, Have and Do
questions.explanation: The perfect tenses use 'have'; A is false, R is true.

questions.question: Which of the following is a modal auxiliary?
questions.subject: Modal Auxiliaries
questions.explanation: Modals: can, could, may, might, shall, should, will, would, must, ought to.

questions.question: A modal auxiliary is always followed by:

options.D: The base form of the verb (without 'to', except 'ought to')

questions.subject: Modal Auxiliaries
questions.explanation: e.g. 'She can swim', not 'She can swims'.

questions.question: Which sentence expresses ABILITY?
questions.subject: Modal Auxiliaries
questions.explanation: 'Can' (and 'could' in the past) express ability.

questions.question: 'You may leave now' expresses:
questions.subject: Modal Auxiliaries
questions.explanation: 'May' is a formal way of giving permission.

questions.question: 'It might rain this evening' expresses:
questions.subject: Modal Auxiliaries
questions.explanation: 'Might' shows less certainty than 'may'.

questions.question: 'You must stop at the red light' expresses:
questions.subject: Modal Auxiliaries
questions.explanation: 'Must' shows strong obligation.

questions.question: 'He must be tired after the long journey' expresses:
questions.subject: Modal Auxiliaries
questions.explanation: 'Must' can express a confident inference.

questions.question: 'You should visit a doctor' expresses:
questions.subject: Modal Auxiliaries
questions.explanation: 'Should' and 'ought to' give advice.

questions.question: Fill in the blank: 'We ___ respect our elders.'
questions.subject: Modal Auxiliaries
questions.explanation: 'Ought' is followed by 'to'.

questions.question: The negative of 'You must go' meaning 'it is not necessary for you to go' is:

options.B: You needn't go (you don't have to go).

questions.subject: Modal Auxiliaries
questions.explanation: 'Mustn't' means prohibition: it is forbidden.

questions.question: 'You mustn't smoke here' expresses:
questions.subject: Modal Auxiliaries
questions.explanation: Compare 'You don't have to' = not necessary.

questions.question: 'When I was young, I would walk to school every day' — 'would' here expresses:
questions.subject: Modal Auxiliaries
questions.explanation: 'Used to' can also express past habits.

questions.question: 'Would you please open the window?' is:
questions.subject: Modal Auxiliaries
questions.explanation: 'Would' and 'could' make requests polite.

questions.question: Fill in the blank: 'When he was five, he ___ swim across the river.'
questions.subject: Modal Auxiliaries
questions.explanation: 'Could' is the past form expressing ability.

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence:

options.B: She can to drive a car.

questions.subject: Modal Auxiliaries
questions.explanation: Modals take no -s and are followed by the base form.

questions.question: 'You should have told me earlier' expresses:

options.A: Regret or criticism about a past action

questions.subject: Modal Auxiliaries
questions.explanation: Modal + have + past participle refers to the past.

questions.question: Fill in the blank: 'How ___ you insult him like that?'
questions.subject: Modal Auxiliaries
questions.explanation: 'Dare' used as a modal takes no -s and no 'to'.

questions.question:
Match the modal with its meaning in context:
a. can (She can swim)
b. may (May I come in?)
c. must (You must obey the law)
d. should (You should exercise)

1. Obligation
2. Permission
3. Advice
4. Ability
questions.subject: Modal Auxiliaries
questions.explanation: These are the core meanings of the modals.

questions.question:
Consider the statements:
I. 'Mustn't' and 'needn't' have the same meaning.
II. Modal auxiliaries do not take -s in the third person singular.
Which is/are correct?
questions.subject: Modal Auxiliaries
questions.explanation: 'Mustn't' = prohibited; 'needn't' = not necessary.

questions.question:
Assertion (A): 'He can plays chess' is incorrect.
Reason (R): A modal auxiliary is followed by the base form of the verb.

options.A: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
options.B: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
options.C: A is true, but R is false
options.D: A is false, but R is true

questions.subject: Modal Auxiliaries
questions.explanation: Correct: 'He can play chess.'
